change.request: Prevent the not-found suppression middleware from mutating a live request route context, preserving mounted-router parameters and middleware behavior.
change.summary: SupressNotFound must not mutate request route context (go-chi/chi #1220)

unknowns: Whether any external examples or consumers rely on SupressNotFound mutating the request route context.
Whether chi.RouteContext returns a shared live context pointer or a copy, which determines if mutation is observable by mounted routers.
Whether chi.RouteContext returns nil for requests lacking a route context, and how SupressNotFound should handle that case without mutation.
Whether mounted-router parameters are stored in Context.RouteParams or Context.URLParams, and which fields must be preserved.
Whether the fix should use Context.Clone or a shallow field copy to avoid mutating the live route context.
Whether the historical PR introduced a new helper in context.go or mux.go to support non-mutating route matching.
Whether the pinned base commit contains a test file for middleware/supress_notfound.go; none appears in the provided tree sample.
Whether the pinned base snapshot contains an existing middleware/supress_notfound_test.go file, as it is absent from the provided tree sample.

risks.rationale: Copying the route context on every request through SupressNotFound introduces allocation overhead that may affect high-throughput servers.
If chi.RouteContext returns nil for requests without a route context, calling rctx.Routes.Match could panic unless nil handling is added.

Changing SupressNotFound to avoid mutating the route context may alter 404 handling for requests that previously matched after mutation, potentially changing status codes or handler invocation for edge-case routes.
Mutating the live request route context in SupressNotFound can overwrite mounted-router route parameters and alter downstream middleware behavior, causing incorrect routing or parameter loss.
Mutating the live request route context can corrupt mounted-router parameters and alter downstream middleware behavior, causing incorrect route matching or parameter loss.
